title.narrative: Safe spaces and housing support for gender-based violence survivors in Cairo

description.narrative:
The situation of refugee women and girls in Egypt has long been a protection concern. The Sudan crisis, however, deepened the gender fault lines and contributed to a silent crisis among refugee communities. Refugees approach UNHCR daily in Egypt with reports incidents of verbal, physical and sexual harassment, domestic violence, harmful traditional practices, rape, forced and child marriages. Unfortunately, UNHCR’s ability to respond to the increase of cases is curtailed by funding cuts, with gender-based violence (GBV) response capacity dropping a fifth between 2023 and 2024 amid regional crises.
UNHCR’s existing response strategy to refugee women and girls, rests on a two-pronged approach: a robust GBV protection response, including shelter, legal aid, access to psycho-social and mental health support, and support to legislative reform for gender equality and protection against GBV complemented by women’s economic empowerment initiatives to support women refugee and asylum-seekers’ in accessing sustainable livelihoods along the lines of the Women’s Empowerment Principles (WEPS).
This approach lies at the heart of the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework 2024 – 2027 between the UN and the Government of Egypt, which by 2027 aims to ensure that “women and girls realize their rights in the social, health and livelihood spheres, as laid out in the Egyptian Constitution, and their leadership and empowerment are guaranteed in a society free of all forms of discrimination and violence against women and girls.”
